info.name: Siri Ice Cream API
info.description:
Ice cream shop API (Go + Fiber + SQLite).

**How to use**
1. Start the server: `go run ./cmd/server`
2. Open **Auth** and send **Login as Owner**. The token is saved automatically.
3. Send any other request.

**Run everything at once:** right-click the collection → **Run collection** → **Run**. The requests run top to bottom and every one checks its own status code.

Variables: `baseUrl` (default http://localhost:3000), `token` (owner, used by most requests), `ownerToken`, `managerToken`, `cashierToken`, `itemId`, `customerId`, `customerEmail` (all filled in automatically).

request.description: Logs in as cashier. Saves the token in the `cashierToken` variable.

exec: pm.test('Returns a token for cashier', () => pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a('string'));

request.description: Logs in as manager. Saves the token in the `managerToken` variable.

exec: pm.test('Returns a token for manager', () => pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a('string'));

request.description: Logs in as owner. Saves the token in the `ownerToken` variable and in `token`, which the other folders use.

exec: pm.test('Returns a token for owner', () => pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a('string'));
pm.collectionVariables.set('token', body.token); // used by the other folders
pm.test('Error message', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error).to.eql('username and password are required'));

request.description: Case-insensitive, partial match. `choc` finds Chocolate Cone and Double Chocolate Cup.
Saves the new item's id in `itemId`.
Only the fields you send are changed.

exec: pm.test('Fields not sent are unchanged', () => pm.expect(item.price).to.eql(350));
pm.test('Error message', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error).to.eql('price must be greater than 0'));
pm.test('Error message', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error).to.eql('id must be a positive number'));

request.description: Uses a unique email each run. The email is saved in lower case.

exec: pm.test('Email is saved in lower case', () => pm.expect(customer.email).to.eql(customer.email.toLowerCase()));

request.description: Sending the customer's own email again is allowed.

exec: pm.test('Error message', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error).to.eql('a customer with this email already exists'));

item.name: 5. Role permissions
item.description: Shows that the backend enforces the role rules. Uses the tokens saved in folder 1.

exec: pm.test('Error message', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error).to.eql('you do not have permission to do this'));

request.description: After this, the saved `token` stops working. Send Login as Owner again to continue.

exec: pm.test('Error message', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error).to.eql('token has been logged out'));
